system.effect:
Terastalization is a type of enhancement and transformation that affects a Pokémon, blinging it out in a massive jewel. Two prerequisites must be met before a Pokémon can Terastalize: the Trainer must be wearing an Accessory Slot Item called a Tera Orb, and the Tera Orb must have accumulated enough energy to initiate and sustain the phenomenon.

When a Pokémon Terastalizes, its Typing is completely overridden to its Tera Type. A Pokémon’s Tera Type is defined through a Capability denoting which Tera Type it has. The Tera Type for a Pokémon is usually its default Type (or one of its default Types) but through special means a Pokémon can have a different Tera Type or be given a new one. When generated or caught, a Pokémon has an 80% chance for its Tera Type to be one of its default Type(s), and 20% to be any other base Type, including the Stellar-Type. GMs including Types beyond the original 18 and Stellar (like Nuclear and Shadow) can choose to allow Pokémon to have Tera Types beyond the basic 19.

Trainers with Type Sync can change a Pokémon’s Tera Type to match the Type(s) they have access to through Type Sync. Otherwise, GMs are recommended to make “Type Shifters” available to change their players’ Pokémon’s Tera Types, akin to NPC Move Tutors. Consider having this service cost 5000₽.

While Terastilized, a Pokémon cannot have its Typing changed from its Tera Type. A Terastalized Pokémon still receives STAB for its original Types, and receives an extra STAB for its Tera Type (apply the in-system Type STAB Boost effects to the Pokémon). If the Tera Type is the same as one of the original Types, this STAB doubles up (so a move gets +4 DB). When a Pokémon Terastalizes into the Stellar-Type, it still receives STAB for its original Types. The Pokémon then gains a extra STAB bonus for every Type. Once the Pokémon uses a Move of a given Type, it loses that extra STAB for that Type for the remainder of their Terastilization.

Note: the Stellar-Type confers no resistances, but has no weaknesses and no Moves may be Tera Type. Logistically, a Stellar-Type Pokémon has no Type-based weaknesses, though certain Moves and Abilities may allow separate increases in effectiveness.

Terastalization can be triggered on either the Pokémon or the Trainer’s turn as a Standard Action. Once triggered, Terastalization lasts for the rest of the Scene, even if the Pokémon is knocked out. A Tera Orb can only fuel one Terastalization at a time, meaning once a Trainer Terastalizes a Pokémon, they can’t Terastalize until the Tera Orb is recharged.
Note: If a Trainer is incapacitated before the Terastalization activation completely resolves, the Tera Orb’s charge is not expended and the target isn’t Terastalized, but the Trainer still uses their Standard Action.

Note: The Terastal phenomenon is most unexplained in the video games, but is primarily tied to phenomena surrounding the Paldea Region’s Area Zero. Like with Dynamax, it is recommended for GMs to be particularly scrutinizing with how they manage the availability of Tera Orbs and their methods to allow Pokémon to alter their Tera Typing, as Terastalization has the potential for significant mechanical and narrative consequences.
